clue.text: Tell gangster to be relaxed

parts.note: to tell on someone is to inform
Al Capone, the archetypal gangster, gives AL

explanation.surface: Someone tells a mobster to take it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal clothes or manners are casual and easygoing, the opposite of stiff.

clue.text: As guerrilla, I run, followed by gunmen with gun raised

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the joined words are read upwards

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, are the army's gunners
a Luger is a German pistol

explanation.surface: A rebel fighter describes running with armed men holding a pistol aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'raised' turns the gunmen and the gun together upwards, so the regular army ends up hidden inside the guerrilla.
explanation.definitionFit: Guerrillas are irregular troops, fighters outside a regular army, so the phrase works as an adjective.

clue.text: Levy for construction of part of highway?

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are built into something new

explanation.surface: A toll is charged to pay for building a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyover is a bridge carrying one road over another, a structural section of a major road.

clue.text: Ring the changes again? This is what O'Connell wanted

definitions.meaning: bell-ringers peal; to do it again is to peal once more
Daniel O'Connell campaigned to undo the Act of Union between Ireland and Britain

explanation.walkthrough: Daniel O'Connell was the nineteenth-century Irish leader of the movement to cancel the Union with Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as RE-PEAL it means ring again; the plain word means revoking a law, here the Union.

clue.text: Love making trouble over allotment

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: Romance stirs up trouble on the allotment garden.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is, in Britain, a rented garden plot, but here it means a share.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love or worship, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Withdraw from diocese about back end of year

indicators.note: the diocese word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a bishop's see is his diocese

indicators.note: the word for the year's last month is read backwards

parts.note: December, DEC, is the last month

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a diocese towards the close of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the month round, and 'about' sets the bishop's seat around it; 'end of year' wants to be a last letter but means the final month.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to formally withdraw from a federation or body.

clue.text: Remain loyal to reserve

explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means support faithfully; as a noun it is a backup kept ready.

clue.text: Allow little margin for error cooking fettucini

indicators.note: cooking prepares the pasta word, mixing its letters

explanation.surface: A chef preparing pasta has very little time to spare.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut it fine is an idiom for leaving barely enough time or room.

clue.text: Shell city located in valley

indicators.note: the city sits inside the valley word

parts.note: a dale is a valley
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian city

explanation.surface: A shell is found in a city set in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A dariole is a small mould, or the pastry case cooked in it, a sort of shell.

clue.text: Note slight indication of fish

definitions.meaning: ..., or re, is the second note of the sol-fa scale
as in a ... of hope, a faint sign

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a sol-fa note, a glimmer (a ray of hope), and a flat sea fish.

clue.text: In favour of vehicle showing some muscle

parts.note: pro means for
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A supporter of a vehicle shows off his strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A protractor is a muscle that extends a limb or part, so it is one kind of muscle.

clue.text: Present the bride with inadvertent revelation

definitions.meaning: at a wedding the father traditionally hands over the bride
something that unintentionally betrays a secret

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb is the wedding ritual of handing over the bride; the noun is an accidental tell-tale sign.

clue.text: Changing direction made left turn superfluous

indicators.note: the word for going to port is turned backwards

parts.note: a ship ported, turned to port, the left side

explanation.surface: A left turn while changing direction was unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: De trop, from French, means unwanted or more than is needed.

clue.text: Fat boy runs inside

indicators.note: the runs letter goes inside the boy word

parts.note: a lad is a boy
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An overweight lad comes running indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is pig fat used in cooking.

clue.text: Ecstatic or infuriated over evidence of debts?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upwards

parts.note: riled means angered
IOUs are notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: Someone is overjoyed or furious when faced with proof of what is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirious can mean wildly excited and happy, as in delirious with joy.

clue.text: Intimate secrets of the laundry

parts.note: soiled sheets and underwear in the wash, and figuratively private scandal not to be aired in public

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is not to wash one's dirty linen in public, that is, not to air private scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally soiled washing; figuratively embarrassing private matters, from the idiom about washing them in public.

clue.text: Siamese mortgage provider — one of the last to come in

definitions.text: one of the last to come in

parts.note: Tai is the language group, and people, to which Siamese (Thai) belongs
a lender advances mortgages

explanation.surface: A Thai bank lending money for homes is a latecomer.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the tail is the last, weakest batsmen, who come in to bat at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail-ender is a low-order cricket batsman, among the last in to bat.

clue.text: Went short when travelling in Cumbria

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters move about

explanation.surface: Someone went without when on a trip through the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when travelling' rearranges WENT SHORT. Cumbria is a county in England's north-west.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumbria lies in the region of England so named, so anything there is described by the compass phrase.

clue.text: Actual number? Any number is employed in game

parts.note: real means actual
ten is a number
N stands for an unspecified number in maths
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about a real figure leads to any number being used in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Real tennis is the old indoor court game from which lawn tennis derives.
explanation.definitionFit: Real tennis is an ancient racket game played in an enclosed court.

clue.text: Short test of ear internally reveals foreign objects

indicators.note: the ear word goes inside the other piece
short means the word for test loses its final letter

parts.note: an exam is a test
otic means relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A brief hearing test turns up strange items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' docks the test word's last letter and 'internally' sets the ear adjective in the gap; 'reveals' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are things that are strikingly foreign or unusual.

clue.text: About half enclosed, restricted to a particular area

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes about the half word

parts.note: enc is the abbreviation for enclosed, seen on letters
demi- means half

explanation.surface: Roughly half is fenced off, confined to one region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps the letter-writer's abbreviation, as at the foot of a business letter, around the prefix for half.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic disease or species is native or confined to one region.

clue.text: Jug, where we're confined

indicators.note: the answer is held within the words

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a pitcher where we are shut in.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large wide-mouthed water jug.

clue.text: Why punishment?

definitions.meaning: to give someone ... is to scold or punish them

explanation.definitionFit: As a question it asks the reason; as a noun, in the idiom give someone what for, it means a reprimand.

clue.text: I produce notes for officer

definitions.meaning: a brass instrument speaking of itself
formerly the lowest cavalry commissioned officer, who carried the colours

explanation.definitionFit: It is a brass instrument like a small trumpet and also an old rank of cavalry officer.

clue.text: To bishop, I would appear very emotional

parts.note: taken as written
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title
I'd contracts I would

explanation.surface: Someone tells a bishop they would seem highly passionate.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrid describes passionate, intensely emotional affairs.

clue.text: Not cheap, the material used in monument

indicators.note: the letters are raw material made into something new

explanation.surface: Expensive stone goes into a memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a war memorial for those buried elsewhere.

clue.text: Club first used to inflict pain

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
maiden means first, as in maiden voyage

explanation.surface: A club was the first thing used to hurt someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The iron maiden was a spiked cabinet said to have been used for torture.

clue.text: He's full of enmity, principally

indicators.note: principally points to the leading letter of each word

explanation.surface: A man is mostly filled with hatred.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is someone full of hostility, so the whole clue describes such a person.

clue.text: Analyse a hundred and nineteen million miles

parts.note: to parse is to analyse grammatically
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone studies a vast distance of many millions of miles.
explanation.walkthrough: The parsec is really about nineteen million million miles; the clue uses the old British billion loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsec is an astronomical unit of distance of about 3.26 light years.

clue.text: American's tense — prettier when relaxed

indicators.note: relaxed suggests the letters are loosened and rearranged

explanation.surface: An American looks tense but prettier once at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when relaxed' rearranges PRETTIER. American spelling drops the final E of the British form.
explanation.definitionFit: The preterit is the simple past tense, spelt this way in the US.
